key_insight: A weighted machine-learning framework using clinical notes and structured EHR data can uncover cross-modal interactions that improve suicide risk prediction in veterans, especially for lower-risk groups.
clinical_relevance: This could help VA-style risk models use both demographics/clinical variables and narrative psychosocial context to better personalize suicide risk assessment.
method: Analyzed 27,241 veterans using structured EHR data plus clinical note text
Replaced semantic lexicon features with a high-dimensional bag-of-words representation
Used XGBoost and weighted CART-style modeling across 30-, 90-, and 270-day lookback windows
evidence_signal: Across cohorts defined by structured suicide-risk strata, the added interactions improved predictive performance in generalized linear models and reduced the gap versus more complex models.
watch_item: High-dimensional text features can be harder to interpret and may behave differently across sites, so external validation and careful calibration are important before deployment.
paper_title: Personalizing Suicide Risk Assessment: Machine Learning Extraction of Cross-Modal Interactions Between Psychosocial and Demographic Factors in Veterans
